meta.working_title: Every Rank on a Pirate Ship

brief.idea: Climb every rank on a Caribbean pirate ship of 1716, from powder monkey to captain, and learn what each one actually did all day.
brief.angle: Second person: you are the boy, then the sailor, then the officer. Every promotion costs something.
brief.hook_promise: By the end you will know why the captain was the least powerful man aboard in peacetime.

sources.title: Marcus Rediker, Villains of All Nations
Charles Johnson, A General History of the Pyrates (1724)

sections.title: Powder monkey
sections.vo_direction: calm, dry irony; let the pauses breathe

sections.title: Gun drill
sections.vo_direction: quicker, clipped, the rhythm of orders

shots.vo: You are eleven years old, and the first thing you learn on this ship is where the gunpowder lives.

image.prompt: a sloop at anchor in a shallow turquoise bay at dawn, seen from the beach, small figures moving on deck

sfx.prompt: gentle waves lapping a wooden hull, distant gulls

shots.vo: It lives below the waterline, behind a felt curtain, in a room where nobody is allowed to carry an open flame.

image.prompt: pulls aside a heavy felt curtain to peer into a low dark magazine lined with stacked kegs, lantern light from behind a glass panel

shots.vo: Your job is to run. Cartridge case in both arms, up the ladder, along the gun deck, and back down before the gun captain shouts your name again.

image.prompt: sprints along a crowded gun deck hugging a leather cartridge case to his chest, glancing back over his shoulder, gun crews at work on both sides

animate.reason: the run is the whole point of the rank; a still frame reads as posed
animate.prompt: the boy runs toward the camera along the deck, crew members lean aside, the case bounces against his chest

sfx.prompt: bare feet slapping on wooden planks, rope creaking

shots.vo: The case is not heavy. That is the trick. A boy can carry it, so a boy is what they use.

image.prompt: close view of small hands gripping the brass-bound lid of a leather cartridge case, a coil of slow match on the deck beside it

shots.vo: Nobody explains the rules to you. You learn them by watching who gets hit, and for what.

image.prompt: stands very still at the foot of a ladder, looking up at a boatswain who is shouting at another boy, crew members deliberately not watching

shots.vo: You are paid a quarter share, when there is anything to share. Most months there is not.

image.prompt: sits on a coil of rope on the forecastle at dusk counting three coins in his palm, the sea empty behind him

shots.vo: Then one morning the drum beats to quarters, and for the first time the drill is not a drill.

image.prompt: the full length of the gun deck from the stern looking forward, every gun run out, crews frozen mid-motion, hatches open above

sfx.prompt: a single drum beating fast, men shouting, feet on planks

shots.vo: Sponge. Load. Ram. Prime. You do not fire the gun. You keep it fed, and you keep your head below the rail.

image.prompt: crouches beside a gun carriage passing a cartridge up to a bare-chested loader, the gun captain above them with the slow match raised

shots.vo: The gun goes off eighteen inches from your ear. You will not hear properly again until Thursday.

image.prompt: flinches away from the gun with both hands clamped over his ears, mouth open, smoke pouring past him toward the open port

shots.vo: And then you run again. Because the gun is empty, and the magazine is not, and that is the whole of your rank.

image.prompt: seen from behind, a small figure disappearing down a smoke-filled ladderway, the gun deck chaos above him going out of view

music.mood: tense low strings, sparse, a single repeating note

concepts.prompt: a small boy with a cartridge case looks up at a towering gun deck, viewed from below
a ladder of ranks drawn as ship decks stacked on top of each other, the boy at the bottom

titles: Every Rank on a Pirate Ship (1716)
You Are Eleven and Your Job Is Gunpowder
From Powder Monkey to Captain: Every Rank Explained
publish.description: Climb every rank on a Caribbean pirate ship of 1716. What each rank did, what it paid, and what it cost.

facts.claim: Powder monkeys on pirate and naval vessels were typically boys aged 10 to 14.
Pirate articles commonly granted boys a half share; a quarter share is attested but less common.
Felt curtains were used at magazine doors specifically to catch sparks.
